note: The studio's one look for factual shorts, as the opening words of every still prompt (the look block, 40-60 words). A proposal the Owner may change; it is not in his database. The film's visual bible may refine the place, season, weather, light and palette in plain words, never the rendering: a bible that asks for another medium is not read here. No codes, no hex colours and no 'no ...' phrases belong in these words: the image model reads them literally. Chart colours live in the bible's card_palette and reach only the local card compositor. Change the words and bump the version.
rendering: Documentary photograph, natural and unposed, true-to-life colour

slots.place: a real location as it is today
slots.light: soft diffuse daylight from high to one side
slots.palette: slate blue, muted moss green, wet earth brown and stone grey
slots.lens: natural 35mm lens perspective with gentle depth of field
slots.grain: fine film grain and crisp detail

fill: Honest textures of stone, soil, water and weathered cloth.
Clear separation between foreground and background.

finish.note: The finish: what the studio does to a film after its pictures are made, locally and for 0 credits. None of it reaches a model (the image model reads only rendering, slots and fill). captions: the burnt captions' colours as #RRGGBB (text, the word being spoken, numbers), their shadow (opacity 0-1, 0-4 px) and whether the spoken word and numbers are coloured. headline: the hook written at the top for its first seconds (off until the Owner chooses it). grade: every filmed shot pulled toward the hero's light and colour (strength 0-1), an optional .cube LUT in config/luts with its licence (a LUT without a licence is not used) and shared grain (0-10). second_framing: a long spoken scene cut to a closer framing of the same picture (zoom 1.12-1.2). cover: a cover image from the hero still and the hook. editorial_qc_blocking: false keeps the editing checks advisory; true makes them refuse a film. A value that is not valid is not used and the default stands.
